title: World’s Largest Supercomputer v. Biology’s Toughest Problems

reader_summary.headline: Hello and welcome to the A16Z podcast.
reader_summary.overview: Hello and welcome to the A16Z podcast. Today's episode celebrates the 20th anniversary of Folding at Home, the distributed computing project for simulating protein dynamics. Today, folding at home is run on millions of devices, is the world's largest supercomputer and tackle some of biology's toughest problems, including COVID-19.

key_points.text: A16Z general partner, BJ Ponday, who founded Folding at home in his lab at Stanford, joins this episode along.

thesis: The episode discusses the origins and technical challenges of the Folding at Home project, a distributed computing initiative that simulates protein dynamics to solve biology's toughest problems like COVID-19. The speakers explain that while early thinking assumed protein folding required a single supercomputer, the project's breakthrough involved developing algorithms to break down inherently sequential simulations into pieces runnable on millions of independent devices.
